Introduction

Board is designed for scenarios where the same business data needs to be viewed in different ways. Built on Pro Table and DataSet, it provides three view types from a single entry:

  • Table view: Uses Pro Table for browsing, filtering, and batch operations.
  • Card view: Displays records as cards to highlight summary information.
  • Kanban view: Groups records into columns by a single-value field such as status, with column pagination and drag-and-drop interaction.

View the Board demos and API

Board does more than change record layouts. Once customization is enabled, users can create, search, switch, configure, and delete views. The views share fields, query conditions, and business APIs, but may use different DataSet instances while rendering.

Quick Start

The following example starts with a table view. dataSet manages business data, while tableProps defines columns, the query bar, and buttons. These columns and buttons also provide the base configuration for card and kanban views.

import React from 'react';
import { Board, DataSet, Table } from 'choerodon-ui/pro';

const { Column } = Table;

const taskDS = new DataSet({
  primaryKey: 'id',
  autoQuery: true,
  queryFields: [
    { name: 'name', type: 'string', label: 'Task Name' },
    {
      name: 'status',
      type: 'string',
      label: 'Status',
      lookupCode: 'TASK.STATUS',
    },
  ],
  fields: [
    { name: 'id', type: 'string', label: 'ID' },
    { name: 'name', type: 'string', label: 'Task Name' },
    { name: 'owner', type: 'string', label: 'Owner' },
    {
      name: 'status',
      type: 'string',
      label: 'Status',
      lookupCode: 'TASK.STATUS',
    },
  ],
  transport: {
    read: {
      url: '/api/tasks',
      method: 'get',
    },
  },
});

export default function TaskBoard() {
  return (
    <Board
      dataSet={taskDS}
      defaultViewMode="table"
      tableProps={{
        queryBar: 'filterBar',
        buttons: ['add', 'save', 'delete', 'reset', 'query'],
        children: [
          <Column name="id" key="id" />,
          <Column name="name" key="name" sortable editor />,
          <Column name="owner" key="owner" sortable />,
          <Column name="status" key="status" sortable editor />,
        ],
      }}
    />
  );
}

At this point, Board works as a table, but persistent multi-view support is not yet enabled. The complete feature requires customizable, customizedCode, customizedLoad, and customizedSave.

Enabling Multi-view Customization

Global Configuration

It is recommended to configure the customization service once at the application entry:

import { configure } from 'choerodon-ui';

configure({
  customizable: {
    Board: true,
    Table: true,
  },
  customizedLoad: async (code, component, params = {}) => {
    if (component !== 'Board') {
      return null;
    }

    if (params.type === 'default') {
      return request(`/api/board-views/${code}/default`);
    }
    if (params.type === 'list') {
      return request(`/api/board-views/${code}`);
    }
    if (params.type === 'detail') {
      return request(`/api/board-views/${code}/${params.id}`);
    }
    return null;
  },
  customizedSave: (code, customized, component) => {
    if (component === 'Board') {
      return request(`/api/board-views/${code}`, {
        method: 'POST',
        data: customized,
      });
    }
  },
});

Board calls customizedLoad(code, 'Board', params) for three kinds of read operations:

params.type Purpose Expected result
default Initialize the current view The default view object, or null when none exists
list Open the view switcher An array of view objects
detail Switch to a specified custom view The complete view object; params.id is the view ID

Creating, updating, activating, and deleting views all call customizedSave(code, customized, 'Board'). The backend must distinguish these operations according to the project's record-status convention and return view data that can be queried afterward. The core view structure is as follows:

{
  "id": "task-board-card",
  "viewName": "My Card View",
  "viewType": "CARD_VIEW",
  "defaultFlag": 1,
  "dataJson": {
    "cardWidth": 6,
    "displayFields": ["name", "owner", "status"],
    "showLabel": 1,
    "cardLayout": "form"
  }
}

Server-side viewType values are TABLE_VIEW, CARD_VIEW, and KANBAN_VIEW. Board converts them internally to table, card, and kanban. The component library's default local-storage implementation does not support the default/list/detail multi-view protocol required by Board, so production applications should provide their own adapter.

Component Configuration

Assign a stable, unique customizedCode to each business page:

<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  customizedCode="task-board"
  customizable
  autoQuery
  defaultViewMode="table"
  viewVisible={{
    table: true,
    card: true,
    kanban: true,
  }}
  tableProps={tableProps}
/>
  • customizedCode: The unique identifier of the customization configuration. Customization is not enabled without it, even when customizable is true.
  • customizable: The component-level switch, which takes precedence over global customizable.Board.
  • autoQuery: Whether to query automatically after switching to a newly created derived view. The default is false.
  • defaultViewMode: The built-in view type used when the remote service does not return a default view.
  • viewVisible: Controls the switch and creation entries for each view type. Setting it to false only hides entries; it is not an authorization mechanism.

Configuring the Default View

defaultViewProps organizes configuration by view type, but initialization only reads the entry corresponding to defaultViewMode. When changing the default type, also provide the configuration for that type.

<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  customizedCode="task-board"
  defaultViewMode="card"
  defaultViewProps={{
    table: {},
    card: {
      cardWidth: 6,
      displayFields: ['name', 'owner', 'status'],
      showLabel: 1,
      cardLayout: 'form',
      buttonDisplay: 'limit',
      buttonPosition: 'top',
      buttonSecPosition: 'right',
    },
    kanban: {
      groupField: 'status',
      cardWidth: 6,
      displayFields: ['name', 'owner'],
      showLabel: 1,
    },
  }}
  tableProps={tableProps}
/>

cardWidth uses the 24-column grid and accepts 4, 6, 8, or 12. In card view, these values display approximately 6, 4, 3, or 2 cards per row. Fields in displayFields should exist in both the business DataSet and the tableProps column configuration.

Card View

Card fields and record commands mainly come from tableProps. The first Column with a command configuration supplies card commands. Use cardProps to add card interactions or completely customize the card body.

<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  customizedCode="task-board"
  tableProps={{
    buttons: ['add', 'save', 'delete', 'reset', 'query'],
    children: [
      <Column name="name" key="name" sortable editor />,
      <Column name="owner" key="owner" sortable />,
      <Column name="status" key="status" sortable editor />,
      <Column
        key="command"
        header="Actions"
        command={({ record }) => [
          <Button key="open" onClick={() => openTask(record)}>
            View
          </Button>,
          'delete',
        ]}
      />,
    ],
  }}
  cardProps={{
    cardWidth: 6,
    onClick: (_event, record) => {
      openTask(record);
    },
  }}
/>

To replace the card body completely, set cardProps.contentRenderer(viewProps, dataSet). When it is provided, handle field display and interactions yourself instead of relying on the built-in card layout.

Kanban View

Preparing the Group Field

A kanban view groups records by a single-value field. The field must provide option data through lookupCode, lookupAxiosConfig, lookupUrl, options, or an applicable lovCode, and it cannot be a multiple-value field.

const statusOptions = new DataSet({
  paging: false,
  data: [
    { value: 'todo', meaning: 'To Do' },
    { value: 'doing', meaning: 'In Progress' },
    { value: 'done', meaning: 'Done' },
  ],
});

const taskDS = new DataSet({
  fields: [
    { name: 'id', type: 'string', label: 'ID' },
    { name: 'name', type: 'string', label: 'Task Name' },
    {
      name: 'status',
      type: 'string',
      label: 'Status',
      options: statusOptions,
    },
  ],
});

When creating a kanban view, the user selects the group field. Each option value becomes a column, while records without a group value go into the “Ungrouped” column.

Configuring Group Queries and Column Pagination

The kanban view does not simply group the current page of records on the client. It uses two kinds of queries:

  • allDsProps: Loads all groups and the first batch of records for each group.
  • columnDsProps: Loads subsequent pages for one group when the user clicks “Load more”.
<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  customizedCode="task-board"
  autoQuery
  defaultViewMode="kanban"
  defaultViewProps={{
    kanban: {
      groupField: 'status',
      cardWidth: 6,
      displayFields: ['name', 'owner'],
      showLabel: 1,
    },
  }}
  tableProps={tableProps}
  kanbanProps={{
    cardWidth: 6,
    isDragDropDisabled: false,
    allDsProps: {
      transport: {
        read: {
          url: '/api/tasks/kanban',
          method: 'get',
        },
      },
    },
    columnDsProps: {
      dataKey: 'rows',
      totalKey: 'total',
      transport: {
        read: ({ data }) => ({
          url: '/api/tasks/kanban/column',
          method: 'get',
          params: data,
        }),
      },
    },
  }}
/>

Board adds groupingBy=status to the all-groups query. A column query also includes a group condition such as status=todo. In the all-groups response, each record represents one group summary. Assuming rows contains records and total contains the group total, the business data can use the following shape:

[
  {
    "status": "todo",
    "rows": [
      { "id": "1", "name": "Confirm Requirements", "status": "todo" },
      { "id": "2", "name": "Break Down Tasks", "status": "todo" }
    ],
    "total": 12
  },
  {
    "status": "doing",
    "rows": [
      { "id": "3", "name": "Develop Login Page", "status": "doing" }
    ],
    "total": 5
  }
]

Whether the API needs an additional outer pagination object depends on the project's DataSet and global dataKey configuration. Explicitly set dataKey and totalKey in columnDsProps so that column records and totals are read consistently.

Handling Drag and Drop

Board provides drag-and-drop interaction but does not automatically update business records or submit changes. Save the new group and order in onDragEnd, then refresh the board or the affected columns.

kanbanProps={{
  isDragDropDisabled: false,
  allDsProps,
  columnDsProps,
  dragDropContext: ({ kanbanDS }) => ({
    onDragEnd: async ({ draggableId, source, destination }) => {
      if (!destination) {
        return;
      }

      await request(`/api/tasks/${draggableId}/move`, {
        method: 'POST',
        data: {
          fromStatus: source.droppableId,
          toStatus: destination.droppableId,
          targetIndex: destination.index,
        },
      });
      await kanbanDS.query();
    },
  }),
}}

When the target is the “Ungrouped” column, droppableId is _empty. Convert it to null or an empty value according to the business API contract before submitting.

Understanding DataSets in Board

Board reuses the fields, query fields, transport, pagination, and selection settings of the provided dataSet, but the actual instance used by each view is not always the same:

View Actual DataSet
Built-in table view Directly uses the provided business dataSet
Custom table view Creates a derived DataSet from the business dataSet configuration
Card view Creates a derived card DataSet
Kanban view Creates an all-groups kanbanDS, plus an independent column DataSet for each group

Do not assume that save, delete, and query operations always run against the original taskDS. Use onChange to obtain the DataSet for the current view:

<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  onChange={({ record, dataSet, currentViewDS, oldViewDS }) => {
    console.log('Current view type', record.get('viewType'));
    console.log('Original DataSet', dataSet);
    console.log('Current view DataSet', currentViewDS);
    console.log('Previous view DataSet', oldViewDS);
  }}
  onConfigChange={({ config, currentViewDS }) => {
    console.log('Saved card or kanban configuration', config);
    console.log('DataSet using the configuration', currentViewDS);
  }}
  tableProps={tableProps}
/>

onConfigChange is used after card or kanban customization is saved. Table-view customization is mainly handled by Table itself.

Adjusting Buttons and Commands by View

All three views share tableProps.buttons and the command column, but they can be filtered according to the current view:

<Board
  dataSet={taskDS}
  renderButtons={({ buttons, viewMode }) => {
    if (viewMode === 'card') {
      return buttons.slice(0, 3);
    }
    return buttons;
  }}
  renderCommand={({ command, viewMode, record }) => {
    if (viewMode === 'kanban' && record.get('status') === 'done') {
      return command.filter(item => item !== 'delete');
    }
    return command;
  }}
  commandsLimit={2}
  tableProps={tableProps}
/>

Card and kanban views provide built-in handling for common top-level buttons such as add, save, delete, remove, reset, and query. Table-specific buttons such as export, expandAll, and collapseAll do not have equivalent behavior in these views and should be hidden or replaced through renderButtons.

Customization Scope

After the customization service is enabled, users can:

  • Create table, card, and kanban views and set a default view.
  • Adjust card width, view height, displayed fields, and field order.
  • Choose a form or grid layout in card view.
  • Control field labels and the position, alignment, and visible count of commands.
  • Configure multi-field combined sorting.
  • Select the group field in kanban view.
  • Use Table customization for column visibility, order, width, and related settings.

Combined-sort candidates come from fields that have sortable set in tableProps and also exist in the DataSet. The backend query API must recognize the corresponding sorting parameters.

Integration Checklist

  1. Give the business DataSet a stable primaryKey, and keep field names consistent with the tableProps columns.
  2. Use a single-value kanban group field that provides complete options through a lookup or options.
  3. Assign a unique customizedCode to each Board.
  4. Support default, list, and detail in customizedLoad, and handle create, update, default switching, and deletion in customizedSave.
  5. Make the all-groups kanban query return the group value, first batch of records, and total; make the column query support group-based pagination.
  6. Submit group and order changes in business code after drag and drop.
  7. When directly operating on current data, use currentViewDS returned by onChange instead of always referencing the original DataSet.

For more DataSet configuration, see the DataSet documentation. For table features and column configuration, see the Table documentation.
